heading: Isaac The Carpentopod
html:
Isaac The Carpentopod is a walking robot that uses Giliam de Carpentier's Carpentopod Linkage. Isaac's body is fully 3D printed in PLA, his brain is an Arduinio mega paired with an L298N dual motor driver that powers both of Isaac's Gearbox DC Motors. ## Design Isaac was designed in OnShape using the ratios Giliam de Carpentier used in his Walking Table. These rations were generated by Giliam using software that eveloved thousands of leg generations until it found an ideal linkage. Giliam was inspried by Jansen's linkage, a similar linkage designed by kinetic sculptor Theo Jansen for his Strandbeest. Isaac is split into three thirds: the outer two sections house three leg linkages each, while the central section holds the electronics. The leg sections use backplates for each linkage, the backplates keep the legs in place while being attached on beams that run to the central section. The central section has four levels sandwhiched between two large plates, these levels contain the electronics. ## Printing The 3D printing process took around 4 days of on and off printing. During this time I used an estimated 700 grams of filament (PLA). To avoid glue, I would pause prints and insert parts into them, allowing for moving parts that are still kept together. Later in the process I printed the central portions of the robot. Some parts did require PLA glue to attach together. While building I also broke some parts, requiring make-up prints. If you would like to 3d print these parts yourself, please see the 3D Files Folder. ## Building and Iteration While Isaac was mostly built as designed, some things were changed or adapted during the process. For example I switched from hot glue to PLA glue. Another notable change was the introduction of gears to provide more torque. These changes helped make Isaac much better. ## Hackclub Isaac was built for the Hackclub program Macondo. For previous projects, Hackclub provided me with funding and an amazing community. You can see Isaac on Hackclub here.

heading: My Birthday Website
html:
From late April to mid May of 2025 I designed and created a website to convince my family to get me a Mac Mini. I was inspired by Beno Grids and Nev Flynn's Dev Site. I made my site on an old all-in-one computer. ## Design My site featured a four wide gride I used to showcase reasons I wanted my Mac Mini. Each box was a very basic div: rounded corners and a black border. Some boxes also had buttons that took you to differnt parts of the site, this was my first time making these types of buttons. Many boxes had icons and images, this was my first time using Google Fonts Icons to render icons. ## Responsiveness To adapt to smaller screens, I added basic CSS responive web design (RWD) to shrink boxes down and cut the gride width. This was my first time using RWD and it shows. Much of the shrinking is messy and breaks some parts of the site.
